quickAnswer: Missouri does not publish one statewide K–12 attendance calendar. Local school boards adopt district calendars within state opening-date, instructional-time, and weather make-up requirements. A featured comparison of Kansas City, Saint Louis, Parkway, and Rockwood shows August 24 or 25 openings and May 27 or 28 endings, while breaks, early dismissals, staff dates, and return-to-school schedules differ.
about:
Missouri public school calendars are prepared by local school boards rather than issued as one statewide student schedule. State law sets the general opening-date limit, minimum attendance hours, and weather make-up framework. Districts still publish the dates families use: first and last student days, breaks, professional-development closures, early dismissals, conferences, finals, make-up dates, and school-specific schedules.

A featured comparison uses reviewed 2026–27 calendars for Kansas City Public Schools, Saint Louis Public Schools, Parkway Schools, and Rockwood School District. Kansas City, Saint Louis, and Rockwood begin August 24, the earliest general opening date permitted for 2026–27; Parkway begins August 25. Saint Louis ends May 27, while the other districts in this comparison list May 28 as the final districtwide student date.

These calendars also show why a statewide holiday list is not enough. KCPS publishes English, Spanish, and Swahili calendar editions and separates the senior last day from the districtwide last day. Parkway uses three half-day dismissal tiers and distinguishes PK–12 half days from high-school finals. Rockwood publishes high-school late starts and a tiered weather-response framework. SLPS combines student dates with staff operations, high-school finals, early releases, conditional make-up dates, and summer school.
calendarRulesDescription: Missouri establishes the calendar framework; local boards publish the student dates and district-specific rules that families must follow.

calendarRules.label: No statewide student calendar
calendarRules.description: Each local school board prepares an annual calendar with its opening date and planned attendance days. First days, breaks, staff dates, and last days therefore vary by district.

calendarRules.label: At least 1,044 attendance hours
calendarRules.description: Missouri requires a minimum term of 1,044 hours of actual pupil attendance. The minimum is 522 hours for qualifying half-day prekindergarten and kindergarten programs.

calendarRules.label: A 169-day rule applies to certain districts
calendarRules.description: Beginning July 1, 2026, districts located wholly or partly in a charter county or a city with more than 30,000 residents generally must schedule at least 169 school days. A qualifying voter-authorized four-day week has a different 142-day minimum.

calendarRules.label: The general opening date is set by state law
calendarRules.description: A district generally may not open earlier than 14 calendar days before the first Monday in September. For 2026–27, that date is August 24, 2026, unless a statutory exemption applies.

calendarRules.label: Weather planning uses hours and approved AMI
calendarRules.description: District calendars include 36 weather make-up hours. A district with a DESE-approved Alternative Methods of Instruction plan may use AMI for up to 36 hours lost to qualifying exceptional or emergency circumstances instead of making up those hours later.

stateSections.label: Four Reviewed Missouri Calendars, Different Family Schedules
stateSections.content: The reviewed districts share a narrow opening window but not one break pattern or one set of special-day rules. The differences below are taken from district-published 2026–27 calendars.

rows: Multilingual calendars and connected conference / PD closures
Seniors finish April 30; all students finish May 28 with early dismissal
Two-hour early releases, high-school finals, and conditional make-up days
Conference windows are not automatically districtwide no-school periods
Three half-day tiers and separate high-school finals scope
PK–12 half days and grades 9–12 finals do not use the same attendance rule
High-school late starts, level-specific dismissals, and AMI rules
Seniors finish May 7; May 28 is the final K–11 student day
table.footnote: These are reviewed district schedules, not statewide Missouri dates. Open the district page for complete events, source notes, and ICS scope.

stateSections.label: Spring Break and Winter Return Dates Differ Across Missouri Districts
stateSections.content: Among the four reviewed calendars, Parkway and Rockwood schedule their main spring break for March 15–19. KCPS students are out March 22–26 through a four-day Spring Break plus a separate Spring Holiday, while SLPS lists Spring Break for March 29–April 2 and a separate no-school day on March 26. Winter return dates also depend on staff calendars: SLPS resumes January 4, while KCPS, Parkway, and Rockwood resume January 5 after January 4 staff dates.

stateSections.content: Missouri law and DESE guidance establish opening-date, attendance-hour, minimum-day, make-up, and AMI requirements. District calendars remain the sources of record for actual student attendance dates.

planningTips: Use the assigned district and school calendar rather than a statewide holiday list. Missouri sets the framework, but attendance dates are local.
Check the staff day immediately after Winter Break. KCPS, Parkway, and Rockwood students return January 5, while SLPS lists January 4 as School Resumes.
Read the scope of early-dismissal and finals dates. Parkway distinguishes PK–12 half days from grades 9–12 finals, and SLPS publishes separate high-school finals windows.
Treat AMI as instruction, not an automatic day off. District weather responses can change after cumulative closures and according to an approved local plan.
Recheck the official district source after a weather closure or revision. MySchoolDates ICS files are one-time imports and do not update automatically.
commonHolidaysDescription: These labels appear across the reviewed Missouri calendars, but their dates and effects are local. A holiday, staff day, AMI day, early release, and school break should not be treated as interchangeable event types.

faqs.q: Does Missouri have one statewide public school calendar?
faqs.a: No. Missouri law requires local school boards to prepare annual calendars within state rules. First days, breaks, staff dates, early dismissals, weather responses, and last days vary by district and sometimes by school or program.

faqs.q: When do Missouri schools start in 2026?
faqs.a: There is no single statewide start date. In the reviewed 2026–27 collection, Kansas City Public Schools, Saint Louis Public Schools, and Rockwood start August 24, while Parkway starts August 25. August 24 is the general earliest opening date under Missouri law for that school year.

faqs.q: How many instructional hours are required in Missouri schools?
faqs.a: Missouri generally requires at least 1,044 hours of actual pupil attendance. The minimum is 522 hours for qualifying half-day prekindergarten and kindergarten programs. Beginning July 1, 2026, certain districts also have an applicable minimum-day requirement.

faqs.q: Does every Missouri district need 169 school days?
faqs.a: No. The 169-day minimum applies to districts located wholly or partly in a charter county or a city with more than 30,000 residents. A qualifying voter-authorized four-day-week district has a separate 142-day minimum. All districts remain subject to the applicable instructional-hour rules.

faqs.q: Do Missouri districts have the same Spring Break?
faqs.a: No. Among the reviewed 2026–27 calendars, Parkway and Rockwood list March 15–19, KCPS students are out March 22–26, and SLPS lists Spring Break for March 29–April 2 with a separate no-school day on March 26.

faqs.q: What is an AMI day in Missouri?
faqs.a: AMI means Alternative Methods of Instruction. A district with a DESE-approved AMI plan may provide instruction outside the normal in-person setting for qualifying closures. An AMI day is an instructional day, not automatically a vacation or a future make-up day.

faqs.q: Can I add a Missouri school calendar to Google Calendar?
faqs.a: Yes. Reviewed Missouri district pages provide ICS files for Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook. Each import is a one-time snapshot and will not automatically reflect later district or school revisions.
